newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rosenthal cuts 96 loss to 4.6 million marks.
newsitem.headline: Rosenthal cuts 96 loss to 4.6 million marks.

text.p: German porcelain manufacturer Rosenthal said on Friday that it had narrowed its loss in 1996 to 4.6 million marks ($2.7 million) from 15.9 million marks, as restructuring continues apace at the group.
The group, which is building up a strategic alliance with Ireland's Waterford Wedgwood, said in a compulsory statement that turnover was down at 320.4 million marks in 1996 from 330.4 million marks.
Rosenthal said that it had reserved some 40 million marks to pay for further restructuring measures.

"Because of changes in the company and as a result of the structural crisis at the group which has yet to be resolved, we think it necessary to introduce further restructuring measures which will hit earnings in 1996," the group said.
The group said it had confirmed a capital rise at a meeting of its supervisory board. This would involve the issue of 300,000 shares at 120 marks, on a ratio of nine shares to four shares.

The issue was guaranteed by Waterford Wedgwood, which holds a 9.1 percent stake in Rosenthal, although the Bavarian bank Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechselbank (Hypo-Bank) did not give its guarantee when the issue was initially proposed at the end of January.
However, Hypo-Bank, which holds a 9.9 percent stake in the porcelain-maker, announced later on Friday morning that it too would be taking part in the capital raise.
Shares in Rosenthal were up two marks at 130 marks in bourse trade in Frankfurt on Friday.
